title: Add an urgent card
prompt: Card is supplied. Finish UrgentCard, which is a Card with a number of Hours. Its Label() returns the title and the hours in the form "Ship (within 4 h)", and that version must also run when the card is held in a Card variable. Then finish Cards.Labels so it returns the Label() of every card, in order.
hints: What does the constructor still have to store, and what does : base(title) already take care of?
Card marks Label as virtual. Which word replaces a virtual method in a derived class?
Add public override string Label() to UrgentCard. In Labels, call Label() on each card, not Title.
support: static Card AsCard(string title, int hours) => (Card)(object)new UrgentCard(title, hours);
checks: Cards.Labels(new List<Card> { new Card("Pack"), AsCard("Ship", 2) }).SequenceEqual(new List<string> { "Pack", "Ship (within 2 h)" })
checkLabels: An urgent card's label must be its title and hours, as in "Ship (within 4 h)".
Calling Label through a Card variable must still give the urgent text.
An urgent card must keep its title.
Hours must hold the hours passed to the constructor.
Labels must return each card's own label, in order.
An empty list must give an empty list.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Declares Label without override, so it only hides the base method.
Reads Title in the loop instead of calling Label().

feedback: If the label is right on an UrgentCard variable but wrong through a Card variable, check for the word override. Then check what Labels reads from each card.
